specification.text: Precompute train-only within-window co-consumption counts C_ij, PMI-like a_ij=clip(log((C_ij+eps)*T/((C_i+eps)(C_j+eps))),-a_max,a_max). For a minibatch items i and K1 parent prototypes y_k on Poincare ball, cost M_ik=d_c(exp_0^c(z_i),y_k)^2 - lambda sum_{j in batch} a_ij softmax_k(-d_c(exp_0^c(z_j),y_k)^2/tau). Compute entropic transport P=Sinkhorn(exp(-M/epsilon), row mass 1/B, column mass target rho_k) where rho has 16–64 active groups, then use soft parent tangent mu_i=log_0^c(sum_k P_ik y_k / sum_k P_ik) (projected weighted ball mean) as context: r'_i=log_0^c(exp_0^c(r_i)⊕_c exp_0^c(g(mu_i))). Quantize r' with Poincare child assignments. Anneal Sinkhorn temperature only on the fixed schedule; final SID uses hard nearest parent and deterministic collision extension.

ideas.title: Behaviour-weighted hyperbolic balanced prefix assignment

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set b_i=0 for all items and use identical Poincare residual quantizers, data, seeds and schedule; this isolates the value of the training successor chart.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use cached training-only P_ij barycenters and the specified fixed-curvature Poincare chart transport and T2/T3 geodesic assignment; train exactly 3,000 Stage2 epochs and evaluate frozen Stage3 protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Retain P_ij and chart-conditioned residual coordinate construction in a matched tangent Euclidean implementation (ordinary vector mean, subtraction/addition and squared Euclidean distance); match scale on training batches and retain codebook sizes/schedule.
ideas.behavior_computation: Count consecutive item pairs only within each user's training interaction sequence, in timestamp order; smooth outgoing counts with alpha times the training-only global item frequency pi. Drop self-pairs if the production preprocessing does so; retain no validation/test events.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed, popularity-smoothed next-item transition distribution P_ij.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute sparse P rows and b_i once, O(T+N*3*degree*D); no sequence scans during training. Per item-step adds two log/exp maps and up to 2*K geodesic evaluations at each of T2/T3 (O(B*K*D), B≈1,023; same asymptotic assignment cost). At 24 steps/epoch and 3,000 epochs: 72,000 optimizer steps, 24,556*3,000=73,668,000 item presentations; cache lookup only per batch. Expect a modest geometry-kernel overhead, benchmark wall time against matched baseline.
ideas.coupling_equation: k_{i,l}=argmin_k d_{-c}(exp_{b_i}^{-c}(log_{b_i}^{-c}(r_{i,l})), exp_{b_i}^{-c}(q_{l,k}))^2, with b_i=FrechetMean_{-c}(x_j;P_{ij}); the behavior term P_{ij} sets the hyperbolic chart used by the curved term d_{-c}.
ideas.coupling_path: Training successors determine b_i; b_i is the origin for log transport of the current latent and for exp-map reconstruction of every candidate residual codeword; geodesic candidate ranking emits T2/T3. Removing behavior sets b_i=0; replacing geometry removes the chart transport and distance.

Keep only if T3 top-1 reaches about .70, T4 is near-deterministic with improved NLL, prefix survival rises jointly, and frozen Stage3 test_R@10 exceeds .065 and both ablations.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Per-item tangent-chart transform and residual code assignment at T2/T3 during Stage2 quantization/training.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare exp/log maps, weighted Karcher barycenter, Mobius subtraction and geodesic distance at fixed negative curvature -c, initially c=0.5.
ideas.key_change: Build each training item's smoothed successor barycenter, transport its latent to that chart on a fixed-curvature Poincare ball, and quantize the transported residual with geodesic distances at T2/T3. Keep T1 as the existing compact coarse stage; decode residual codewords back through the inverse transport before the next residual is formed.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Construct P, pi, b_i solely from training-split events and frozen training item embeddings; cache by item ID. Validation/test are used only by the existing evaluator after SIDs are frozen and cannot update counts, barycenters, codebooks, or hyperparameters.
ideas.motivation: Items with the same likely next-item neighborhood should share a predictable coarse chart, while the chart should leave a compact, behaviorally coherent residual for T2/T3 rather than forcing continuation detail into T4.
ideas.novelty: Unlike assigning T1 from a successor geodesic consensus score or adding a Busemann direction to a codeword score, the transition signal defines an item-specific tangent chart in which the residual itself is quantized; it changes the coordinates and distances used at T2/T3.
ideas.observables: Report canonical 52,855-pair L1 Hard ER with ten fixed negatives, gold-prefix survival at depths 1-4 in width-20 beam, teacher-forced T3/T4 NLL and top-1, and Stage3 test_R@10. Compare all measures across the three arms.
risks: Sparse/noisy successor rows make barycenters unstable; popular items dominate smoothed means; chart transport can over-normalize distinct items or make residual subtraction inconsistent with the baseline decoder. T1 remains the bottleneck if its compact grouping is not predictive.
ideas.safeguards: Compute geometry in float32; project norms to (1-eps)/sqrt(c), eps=1e-5; use log/exp denominator clamps, Karcher step size <=0.25 and exactly 3 iterations; normalize P with alpha>0 and minimum outgoing mass; fall back to origin for n_i=0; clip tangent norms and verify finite forward/gradients. Use identical fixed negatives and deterministic collision extension in all arms.
ideas.spec_equations: x_j=exp_0^{-c}(z_j); b_i=KarcherMean_{-c}(x_j,P_ij); v_i=log_{b_i}^{-c}(r_i); q*=argmin_k d_{-c}(exp_{b_i}^{-c}(v_i),exp_{b_i}^{-c}(q_k))^2; r_i←MobiusSub_{-c}(r_i,exp_{b_i}^{-c}(q*)). Apply at l=2,3; deterministic T4 collision extension unchanged.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are frozen training item embeddings, sparse training transition counts, current residual, and T2/T3 codebooks; output is the selected residual token, quantized point and next residual. Cache one b_i and confidence per training item.

specification.text: Let training-only P_ij=(n_ij+alpha*pi_j)/(n_i+alpha), where n_ij counts consecutive training events and pi is the training-item frequency distribution. Map frozen item embeddings z_j to x_j=exp_0^c(z_j), project to radius <(1-eps)/sqrt(c), and define b_i=FrechetMean_c({x_j;P_ij}) by 3 weighted Karcher steps. Let a_i=min(1,n_i/n0). At residual level l=2,3, let r_i be the current residual point and v_i=log_{b_i}^c(r_i); assign k=argmin_k d_c(exp_{b_i}^c(v_i), exp_{b_i}^c(q_lk))^2, with q_lk constrained to the tangent ball radius R and the usual straight-through update. Subtract the selected q in the same chart using Mobius subtraction and repeat; level 4 remains deterministic collision extension.

ideas.title: Successor-charted hyperbolic residual transport

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set h_i to its training-set mean and remove p_ij edge consistency, giving all items the same fixed c; retain curved quantization, architecture, schedule and codebook sizes.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use per-item c_i from training-only normalized transition entropy, Poincare exp maps/geodesic assignment at all levels, and the sparse successor geodesic consistency term; run fixed 3,000 epochs and frozen Stage3 evaluation.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Keep h_i, p_ij, and edge weighting but replace exp/log maps and geodesic distances with Euclidean vectors and squared Euclidean distances; use training-only scale matching for the edge term.
ideas.behavior_computation: Count ordered consecutive item transitions inside training user histories only; form additively smoothed p_ij using training-only item-frequency prior pi; compute normalized entropy H/log(max(2,d_i)) over observed plus smoothed successor support. Cache h_i once before Stage2.
ideas.behavior_signal: Normalized entropy/effective branching of the directed next-item distribution.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute H_i,h_i from sparse transition counts O(T+N*degree), negligible cache. Per assignment adds a per-item curvature scale and existing hyperbolic distance cost O(B*K*D); continuation regularizer adds sparse successor-code lookups O(B*degree*D) for sampled edges. Frozen scale: 24,556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3,000 epochs = 72,000 steps and 73,668,000 item presentations; no extra full-catalog pass per step. Expected 5-15% wall-clock overhead depending on sparse edge sampling; measure on the four-card baseline.
ideas.coupling_equation: k_{il}=argmin_k d_{c_i}(exp_0^{c_i}(u_{il}),exp_0^{c_i}(e_{lk}))^2 + lambda*a_i*sum_j p_{ij} d_{c_i}(e_{l,k_{il}},e_{l,k_{jl}})^2, where c_i=c_min+(c_max-c_min)(1-h_i); the behavior term (p_ij,h_i) sets the curvature c_i of the curved assignment and successor score.
ideas.coupling_path: Transition probabilities yield h_i and c_i; c_i determines the exp map and geodesic distance ranking the residual codewords, while those same selected codewords are compared along training successor edges under d_{c_i}. Removing behavior makes curvature constant and removes edge weighting; Euclidean replacement removes both curved map and distance.

ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Normalized continuation entropy predicts how much semantic branching an item actually needs. Curvature conditioned on it will reserve a small, stable prefix for low-branching behavior and use later residual tokens for genuine alternatives, improving joint beam survival rather than just shifting information to T4. Keep only if full run raises joint survival and Stage3 test_R@10 above .065, with T3/T4 metrics moving in the predicted direction versus each ablation.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Every residual assignment in Stage2 and the successor consistency regularizer; c_i is fixed per item from training data and applied to the latent and codebook points.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Item-conditioned Poincare exponential map and geodesic codeword distance with negative curvature -c_i, plus geodesic distance in the continuation consistency term.
ideas.key_change: Estimate each item's effective successor branching and use it to condition the negative curvature in a shared Lorentz/Poincare hierarchical quantizer. Low-branching items receive stronger negative curvature (more radial separation and a short predictable hierarchy); high-branching items receive flatter curvature and retain more angular/residual capacity, with a training-only regularizer preventing the four-level path from pushing all detail to T4.
ideas.leakage_boundary: All pair counts, prior frequencies, entropy values, and any sampled successor edges come exclusively from training histories. Freeze cached h_i before validation or test evaluation; no interaction, metric, or target from those splits can enter curvature, assignments, or regularizer.
ideas.motivation: A single global curvature and residual scale spend too many tokens distinguishing items with many competing continuations, while low-branching items need a compact, easily predicted prefix and a decisive tail.
ideas.novelty: Existing transition methods use successor direction, geodesic consensus, or boundary potentials to choose/steer codes. This instead uses a training-only continuation branching statistic to set the curvature of an item-conditioned hyperbolic quantization metric, then lets the resulting radial hierarchy shape all four assignments; it does not append a behavior token or merely change codebook size.
ideas.observables: Evaluate canonical 52,855-pair L1 Hard ER (ten fixed negatives), gold-prefix survival depth 1-4 at beam width 20, teacher-forced T3/T4 NLL and top-1, and Stage3 test_R@10. Predict L1 ER flat or slightly lower with 16-64 effective groups, L1 survival up, then survival retained/improved at T2-T4; T3 top-1 near/above .70, T4 NLL lower and top-1 near deterministic; test_R@10 must exceed .065. Explicitly inspect whether gains are joint rather than a T4-only information shift.
risks: Entropy may mostly measure item popularity/data sparsity; per-item curvature can create discontinuous code boundaries, overfit rare items, or cause optimizer scale mismatch. The balance penalty may trade reconstruction accuracy for an artificial token distribution; hyperbolic effective dimension may be insufficient.
ideas.safeguards: Smooth counts with alpha>0 and cap maximum successor support; use h_i=1 for no data and confidence a_i=min(1,n_i/n0); clamp c_i to [.15,1], project all ball norms below (1-eps)/sqrt(c_i), eps=1e-5; float32 geometry and finite-gradient checks. Sample a fixed maximum number of successors per item with deterministic training-only sampling; stop gradients through argmin and neighbor IDs. Estimate conditional entropy penalty only on adequately populated training prefixes, with pseudocounts and clipped penalty; keep seeds/schedule/negative set fixed.
ideas.spec_equations: p_ij=(n_ij+alpha*pi_j)/(n_i+alpha); H_i=-sum p_ij log p_ij; h_i=clip(H_i/log(max(2,d_i)),0,1); c_i=cmin+(cmax-cmin)(1-h_i); x_il=exp_0^{c_i}(u_il); k_il=argmin_k d_{c_i}(x_il,exp_0^{c_i}(e_lk))^2; L=L_RQVAE+lambda*a_i*sum_j p_ij*d_{c_i}(e_{k_i},e_{k_j})^2+lambda_b*relu(H(T3|T1,T2)-H(T4|T1,T2,T3)-m).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are training-only sparse successor counts/prior, cached h_i and confidence a_i, current residual vectors, and four existing codebooks. Output is four fixed-width tokens (with existing deterministic collision extension) and the standard reconstruction/commitment plus behavioral regularizer losses.

specification.text: From training transitions define p_ij=(n_ij+alpha*pi_j)/(n_i+alpha), H_i=-sum_j p_ij log p_ij, and h_i=clip(H_i/log(max(2,d_i)),0,1), with h_i=1 when no evidence. Let c_i=c_min+(c_max-c_min)*(1-h_i), c_min=.15,c_max=1.0, differentiable only through latent/codebooks (c_i cached). At each level l map residual u_il to Poincare x_il=exp_0^{c_i}(u_il), assign k by argmin d_{c_i}(x_il,exp_0^{c_i}(e_lk))^2. Add a training-only continuation consistency penalty lambda*a_i*sum_j p_ij min_{k in N(k_i)} d_{c_i}(e_{l,k_i}, e_{l,k_j})^2 on the first three-level prefix representatives, where N maps successor item codes through the same current codebooks; stop-gradient through the discrete neighbors. Add a tail-balance penalty lambda_b*relu(H(T3|T1,T2)-H(T4|T1,T2,T3)-m) estimated over training batches, preventing excess ambiguity from being deferred to T4.

## What the seven measured arms show (Issue #125 forensics, 57,439 rows, width-20 beam)

Every number below is measured on the frozen checkpoints with the production evaluator.
"coverage" is the share of rows whose target SID survives among the twenty beams;
"alive" is the share whose gold prefix is still alive at that depth; acc@1 is the
teacher-forced top-1 accuracy of that position.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| l1_only | 0.06233 | 0.0855 | 1.000/.829/.156/.086 | 1.000/.175/.106/.557 | 1/94/256/37 |
| l1_br_euclid | 0.06207 | 0.0847 | 1.000/.829/.161/.085 | 1.000/.178/.115/.550 | 1/80/256/44 |

**The measured rule.** Recall@10 is ordered by coverage and by nothing else, and coverage
is the *joint* survival of the four positions. Two ingredients exist, and no arm has both:

1. **A coarse first level is free.** `successor_geodesic_coarse` put 26 codes in T1 and its

   rows drop there) and its coverage only reached 0.0740.
2. **A decisive tail is what pays.** `resample` has the *worst* first-token survival of all
   arms (0.497, T1 acc 0.098) and still the best coverage, because its third token is
   correct 79.4% of the time given the oracle prefix and its fourth token 97.7% of the

`successor_geodesic_coarse` combined with the tail ratios of `resample` would give a
coverage near 0.17 instead of 0.088, i.e. roughly double the best arm.

## What this round must design

A mechanism whose **joint survival** is maximised: a first level that is cheap to predict
*and* behaviourally meaningful, plus a tail that is decisive. Concretely, the proposal
must aim for a first level of roughly 16-64 effective groups whose gold token survives
almost always, and for the later positions to be nearly determined by the earlier ones
(T3 top-1 around 0.7 or better, T4 nearly deterministic over a small extension alphabet),
while keeping a genuine behaviour-conditioned hyperbolic computation and a train-only
behaviour signal on one connected path.

The behaviour conditioning may act on the first-level assignment, on the residual path
that feeds T2/T3, or on both; what matters is that it *changes the curved computation*
that produces the tokens, and that the proposal states why the coupling makes the later
tokens more predictable rather than merely different. A mechanism that only renumbers the
first level, or that only pushes the information into T4, is out of scope.

A plain codebook-size change is out of scope; a curved assignment with no behaviour term
is out of scope.

Propose two or three ideas from *different* coupling sites, for example: a coarse hyperbolic
first level whose prototypes are placed by the train-only successor structure together with
a residual-level coupling; a curved assignment whose *second* level inherits the behaviour
prototype through the tangent transport; a hierarchical geometry where one behaviour
prototype steers the first level and the residual transport, so the third code becomes a
near-deterministic function of the first two.

Each idea must state its three arms (both-on, behaviour-off, geometry-off) and the predicted
direction of: `L1 Hard ER` on the canonical 52,855 pairs with ten fixed negatives,
gold-prefix survival at depths 1-4 under width-20 beam search, the teacher-forced NLL and
top-1 accuracy of T3 and T4, and Stage 3 `test_R@10` (target > 0.065).

## Frozen constraints

Four-token fixed-width SID with the deterministic collision-extension token, 3000 Stage 2
epochs on four cards, no early stopping, no test-time tuning, the frozen Stage 3 protocol,
and no validation or test behaviour in SID construction.

Our experiments demonstrate that HyperVQ matches traditional VQ in generative and reconstruction tasks, while surpassing it in disc

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. Hyperbolic geometry offers a natural alternative for hierarchical representations, but naive hyperbolic extensions introduce geometric inconsistencies: non-associative hyperbolic addition prevents consistent residual aggregation, while standard straight-through gradient estimation ignores the geometry of the latent space. We propose a geometry-aware hyperbolic residual quantization that addresses these issues in both the forward and backward passes. In the forward pass, Hyperbolic Residual Aggregation restores the telescoping behavior of residual quantization on the Poincare ball. papers.abstract: Most high-performance block-coding systems for image compression, such as JPEG, have been designed for software or dedicated digital hardware implementations where the data are already assumed to be available in digital format. In modern CMOS photosensors, smart-pixel technologies have allowed the realization of basic signal processing tasks at the pixel level, in analog format before analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion. The elimination of A/D converters and implementation of block-coding directly over analog blocks of pixels in such sensors can be attractive both in terms of area savings and power consumption. The design of block encoders, under the strong hardware constraints that derive from the A/D converter removal, has been investigated in this paper. We present a comparison of three systems in terms of rate, distortion and complexity, and present a numerical simulation analysis of their sensitivity to implementation errors. papers.title: Sensitivity analysis of low-complexity vector quantizers for focal-plane image compression

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
papers.title: Representation Collapsing Problems in Vector Quantization

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. Such algorithms typically use gradient descent with backpropagation and the chain rule. Hence, the backpropagation fails if intermediate gradients are zero for some functions in the computational graph, because it causes the gradients to collapse when multiplying with zero. Vector quantization is one of those challenging functions for machine learning algorithms, since it is a piece-wise constant function and its gradient is zero almost everywhere. A typical solution is to apply the straight through estimator which simply copies the gradients over the vector quantization function in the backpropagation. Other solutions are based on smooth or stochastic approximation. This study proposes a vector quantization technique called NSVQ, which approximates the vector quantization behavior by substituting a multiplicative noise so that it can be used for machine learning problems.
